messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PAGERDUTY-6421 fired for service=embeddings-us-west — alert: 5xx rate > 10% (3m)

pagerbot: @here Page auto-fired (priority: high). Escalation path: oncall -> SRE rotation. Use /ack to claim.

Anna M.: acked? anyone oncall able to grab this? looks like multiple dup pages just queued.

Sam (oncall): grabbing it now — /ack from pagerbot. I'll take ownership for initial triage :hand:

pagerbot: Sam (oncall) has acknowledged the page and is the current owner. PD incident: PD-6421

Miguel S.: Sam — thanks. quick q: is this an outage or elevated errors? any customer-facing symptoms yet?

Sam (oncall): initial glance: high 5xx from embeddings ingestion path in us-west. Errors spike at 14:02 UTC. Latency up but some requests still succeed. No SLO breach yet but error budget burn if persists.

Sam (oncall): logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:21Z embeddings-worker-12 ERROR "kv-cache: failed to open shard" status=500 trace_id=tx-9f3a
2026-03-15T14:02:23Z frontend-proxy-3 WARN "upstream 5xx rate" path=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large 5xx=12.3%
```

Katie L.: saw duplicate alerts — PD sent three pages in 90s for same symptom. Could be suppression not catching this sequence. Noted: customers on some Hosted API keys in us-west seeing transient fails.

Anna M.: adding customer impact note — Support: TENANT-118 and TENANT-203 reporting errors in logs. ETA: waiting on internal mitigation.

Miguel S.: Sam, can you check worker pool health and queue depth? runbook step 1-3 applies (embeddings-queue/restart-workers)

Sam (oncall): running quick checks. queue depth: 98k (norm 12k). workers: 78 running, 12 in CrashLoopBackOff. Suspect upstream KV shard flaps. Kicking off rolling restart on embeddings-workers-pool us-west. Command:
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/embeddings-workers -n prod-us-west --timeout=5m
```

Sam (oncall): also toggling routing to prefer eu cluster for requests from high-value customers while we stabilize (temporary). Applying route override now.

pagerbot: Note: modifying route overrides may impact latency. Confirm with :thumbsup: before proceeding.

Anna M.: :thumbsup: go ahead. notify support of degraded errors + routing change.

Sam (oncall): restart in progress — patching config and restarting pods. ETA ~3-4m per batch. Will report back after first batch.

(2m later)

Sam (oncall): batch 1 restarted. CrashLoopBackOff count decreased from 12 -> 4. queue depth down to 72k. 5xx rate moved from 12.3% -> 6.1% in the window.

Miguel S.: good signal. can you capture a heap/profile from one of the failing pods? also collect metrics for KV shard errors for postmortem.

Sam (oncall): grabbing core/profile and uploading to S3: s3://redwood-ops/pd-6421/profiles/ (link posted to PD incident soon)

pagerbot: PD-6421 updated: owner=Sam, status=mitigating, ETA=20m for full recovery. Duplicate pages suppressed for now.

Anna M.: pinging support: message sent to TENANT-118 and TENANT-203 — "We're mitigating a transient embeddings failure in us-west; traffic may be routed to eu temporarily. We'll follow up with timeline."

Support-Bot: Tenant notifications delivered (TENANT-118, TENANT-203).

Katie L.: quick ask — is this likely caused by recent kernel update on the node pool? saw kubelet restarts in infra logs at 13:58.

Miguel S.: infra note: there was an autoscaler event around 13:55 that rescheduled shards; could correlate. Will check infra logs and node reprovisioning timeline.

Sam (oncall): batch 3 finished. CrashLoopBackOff now 0, queue down to 18k, 5xx at 1.7% (close to baseline). Rolling restart completed.

Sam (oncall): mitigation succeeded for now. I'm going to keep PD incident open for 1 hour to monitor. If stable, will hand back to next rotation.

Anna M.: thanks Sam. can you do a handoff when you drop ownership? want notes for postmortem: initial cause suspected KV shard instability + possible autoscaler timing + duplicate-page chatter in PagerDuty.

Sam (oncall): handoff plan:
- keep monitoring 1h
- collect pods profiles + KV shard logs (uploaded)
- follow-up ticket: OPS-2145 with timeline and mitigation steps
- handoff to Miguel at 15:30 UTC if stable

pagerbot: Reminder: use /handoff <user> to transfer PD ownership when ready.

(Monitoring window)

Sam (oncall): 30m stable. 5xx < 1% for 25m. Queue steady. I'll /handoff Miguel S. in 5.

Sam (oncall): /handoff @Miguel S.

pagerbot: PD-6421 ownership transferred: previous_owner=Sam (oncall) new_owner=Miguel S. Status=monitoring. Handback note: "Rolling restart resolved pod crashes; collecting KV shard logs; follow with infra review + suppression tuning." 

Miguel S.: taking it — thanks Sam. I'll own the follow-up and coordinate with infra to root cause. filing OPS-2145 now and linking PD incident + S3 artifacts.

Miguel S.: filed OPS-2145: https://redwood.internal/ops/OPS-2145 (contains timeline, artifacts, recommended actions: k8s node drain policy tweak, PD suppression window adjustment, kv-shard healthchecks)

Anna M.: marking internal customer comms draft ready. We'll send a post-incident note once Miguel signs off on RCA.

Support-Bot: Support tickets updated with latest note and mitigation summary.

Miguel S.: leaving a final status ping: PD-6421 set to "monitoring" and will be closed after infra completes node review. Estimated RCA ETA: 48h.

Anna M.: thx all. closing chat for now — please add any follow-ups to OPS-2145. :white_check_mark:
